name: From Standalone LLMs to Integrated Intelligence: A Survey of Compound AI Systems (CAIS)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2506.04565, cs.MA/cs.CL; v1 Jun 2025, v2 May 2026). Indexed by Semantic Scholar/DBLP as a Review/JournalArticle; no peer-reviewed venue identified.
authors_affiliation: Jiayi Chen, Junyi Ye, Guiling Wang -- all at New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT), Newark, NJ, USA.
code_url: N/A (literature survey; no official code repository associated)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no maintained GitHub paper list / leaderboard found; the survey is a frozen PDF with no companion living repo)
task_domain: Survey spanning QA, tool-use, decision-making/agents, multimodal (vision/audio/video), code, and web; organizes the field of LLM-augmented compound systems rather than solving a single task.
problem_setting: A systematic literature survey (not an empirical method). It defines Compound AI Systems (CAIS) as a framework integrating one or more LLMs (L), external components (C: retrievers, tools, agents, multimodal encoders, prompt-engineering, self-optimization), and a system design (D: orchestration/topology), formalized as f(L,C,D). Settings covered include offline RAG pipelines, interactive single- and multi-agent loops, multimodal perception, and orchestrated multi-component pipelines. Supervision varies by surveyed work. Search ran Dec 2024-May 2026 over ACM DL, arXiv, IEEE Xplore, Semantic Scholar covering 2020-early 2026; ~400 candidates screened to 220+ papers retained (227 references).
what_is_retrieved: Primarily documents/passages and external knowledge (open-domain corpora, knowledge-graph triples, KBs) in the RAG axis; tools/APIs in the agent and orchestration axes; and multimodal context (encoded image/audio/video tokens) in the MLLM axis. As a survey it catalogs these retrieval targets rather than retrieving itself.
retrieval_grounding: Predominantly STATIC external corpus (docs/KB/APIs) for the RAG axis; the survey also covers HYBRID grounding where orchestration adds memory management (e.g., KV-cache via PagedAttention) and agents draw on tool registries. Growing/episodic agent memory is acknowledged but is not the survey's central retrieval framing.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Mostly a fixed top-k ranking objective for RAG retrievers (the survey discusses recall/precision/nDCG/MRR top-k retrieval quality). Tool-retrieval for large registries (active tool discovery, e.g., Fei et al. 2025 extending MCP) edges toward needed-set selection, but the survey does not frame a formal completeness objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey does not frame any axis as case-based reasoning; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle is discussed)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False -- the survey does not frame itself or surveyed systems as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: Heterogeneous across axes as catalogued: token/snippet and document/passage (RAG dense/sparse retrieval), knowledge-graph triples / KG-subgraph (graph retriever, e.g., KAPING, GraphRAG), tool-API schemas (agent/orchestration tool use, MCP tools), and multimodal token embeddings (MLLM encoders). Document/passage is the dominant RAG retrieval unit.
index_source: Mainly static offline-built corpora/vector indices for RAG (pre-retrieval: chunking, embedding, indexing). The survey also covers live/dynamic tool indices via MCP and active tool discovery (Fei et al. 2025) and KV-cache memory (PagedAttention), i.e., hybrid static-plus-runtime stores. No single induced store -- it is a meta-level catalog.
index_structure_topology: Catalogs multiple topologies: flat vector index (dense retrieval), sparse term index (BM25), knowledge GRAPH index (graph retrievers / GraphRAG / KAPING), and hierarchical/modular component organization in orchestration (structural layer: hierarchical and centralized structures). Tool registries are organized for retrieval/discovery (MCP servers).
retriever_type: Survey explicitly classifies retrievers into five types: Sparse (BM25), Dense (BERT-style embeddings), Graph (KG traversal), Hybrid (sparse+dense), and LLM-as-Retriever. Also a two-dimension framing (Phase: pre-retrieval/retrieval/post-retrieval; Approach: the five functional types).
retriever_learning_signal: Spans the spectrum across surveyed work: off-the-shelf (BM25), contrastive/dense similarity training, LM-feedback and downstream-effectiveness co-training/dual fine-tuning of retriever+generator (e.g., RAG-end2end, Atlas/T5, REPLUG), and query-rewriting learned via trainable rewriters (Ma et al. 2023). No single signal -- the survey enumerates them.
query_construction: Catalogs raw query, query rewriting (trainable rewriter), query preprocessing/expansion, docid-based mapping (DSI), thought-conditioned queries in iterative/recursive RAG (IRCoT, ITER-RETGEN), and self-reflection-driven decisions (SELF-RAG). Multimodal queries are encoded into vectors that drive the RAG retriever in the unified pipeline.
query_granularity: Both task-level (one-shot retrieval at query time, classic RAG) and step/iteration-level (iterative ITER-RETGEN, recursive IRCoT chain-of-thought, adaptive SELF-RAG) are covered. The survey contrasts one-shot vs iterative/recursive/adaptive patterns.
when_to_retrieve: Survey contrasts one-shot retrieval, iterative (repeated retrieve-generate cycles), recursive (nested decomposition), and adaptive (dynamically decide when to retrieve, e.g., SELF-RAG self-reflection). Covers the full one-shot/iterative/active/adaptive space as a RAG-design taxonomy axis.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Catalogs fixed-schedule retrieval (standard RAG), iteration-driven triggers (ITER-RETGEN/IRCoT), and learned/self-reflective triggers (SELF-RAG reflection tokens deciding when to retrieve and critique). In agents, retrieval/tool calls are agent-initiated within ReAct-style loops; orchestration may trigger additional retrieval via feedback arcs.
reranking: Yes -- explicitly part of the Post-Retrieval phase: reranking reorders/reassesses retrieved results to maximize relevance (cites Lazaridou et al. 2022, Glass et al. 2022, Ram et al. 2023). Also lists knowledge filtering and refinement as post-retrieval steps. Specific reranker architectures (cross-encoder etc.) are referenced rather than prescribed.
retrieved_context_refinement: Survey enumerates post-retrieval refinement: knowledge filtering (constraint-based search-space reduction), knowledge refinement (coherence/usability improvement), and reranking. Generator-side filtering (fine-tuned to keep relevant docs and discard irrelevant ones, e.g., Yoran et al. 2023) is also covered as distractor filtering.
tool_document_engineering: Covered at a survey level: tool schemas standardized via function-calling / OpenAPI and MCP (resources, prompts, tools, sampling). Mastouri et al. 2025 auto-compile OpenAPI REST APIs into MCP servers; Fei et al. 2025 add active tool discovery so agents retrieve relevant tools from large registries instead of dumping static schemas into the context window.
index_content_separation: Discussed implicitly: Fei et al. 2025 (active tool discovery over MCP) retrieves relevant tools from registries rather than loading all schemas into context -- a lightweight-index-then-load pattern. Not framed as a formal SOP-index-then-content principle for RAG.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Yes, a notable theme in Section 8.5 (Standardization). Covers static schema layer (structured tool interfaces / function-calling / OpenAPI), the Model Context Protocol (MCP, Anthropic Nov 2024; host/client/server over JSON-RPC 2.0; resources/prompts/tools/sampling) as a live tool-access protocol with active discovery, and agent-interoperability protocols (A2A, ACP, ANP).
tool_dependency_awareness: Limited. The survey discusses orchestration topology (hierarchical/centralized) and model communication, and tool-access protocols, but does not center inter-tool dependency modeling (output-of-A feeds B / dependency graphs) as a distinct retrieval mechanism. [uncertain]
how_retrieved_used: Catalogs prompt augmentation (injecting retrieved context into the generator), training-signal use (co-training / dual fine-tuning of retriever+generator, RL-trained generators), modular augmentation (REPLUG keeps LLM frozen), and tool-result injection in agent/orchestration loops. Multimodal tokens are fused into the LLM context.
planning_integration: Surveyed across patterns: retrieve-then-generate (one-shot RAG), iterative/recursive interleaving of retrieval with chain-of-thought reasoning (IRCoT, ITER-RETGEN), adaptive self-reflective retrieval (SELF-RAG), per-step tool calls inside ReAct-style agent loops, and orchestration-scheduled retrieval/tool triggers in a feedback loop (the unified CAIS pipeline, Figure 1).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Survey spans per-answer (vanilla RAG), per-CoT-step / per-iteration (IRCoT recursive, ITER-RETGEN iterative), reflection-token-gated (SELF-RAG), and per-tool-call within an agent rollout (ReAct loops, orchestration feedback). No single granularity -- it is a taxonomy axis.
retrieved_item_representation: Catalogs raw retrieved passages/documents injected into prompts, KG triples (graph retrieval), tool/API call results, and multimodal token embeddings. The survey treats surface form descriptively rather than proposing a distilled/latent representation.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mostly raw retrieved passages/documents and KG triples (low abstraction); also tool-API descriptions and multimodal embeddings. The survey does not emphasize distilled strategies/skills as retrieved units (that is more an agent-memory framing outside its central RAG taxonomy).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Covers generator-side filtering fine-tuned to discard irrelevant retrieved docs (Yoran et al. 2023, Zhang et al. 2024, Luo et al. 2023), post-retrieval knowledge filtering, self-reflection/critique (SELF-RAG a priori/a posteriori judgment, Ren et al. 2023), and reranking to demote distractors. Faithfulness/Context-Precision metrics (Ragas) used to measure robustness.
memory_type: Catalogs several: none (stateless RAG), KV-cache/working memory managed at the system level (PagedAttention), and orchestration-level memory management; multi-agent shared state. Episodic/skill-library agent memory is acknowledged but not a deeply developed dedicated taxonomy axis in this survey.
write_back: Survey-level: not a defining theme. The orchestration memory-management discussion centers on resource allocation (KV-cache paging) rather than writing new experiences/cases back into a retrievable store. The survey itself does not write back. [uncertain]
online_growth: Touched on via dynamic/live tool indices (MCP active tool discovery) that can grow at deployment, but the survey does not center test-time growth of an episodic experience store. Mostly static RAG corpora are assumed. [uncertain]
write_back_trigger: Not a focus of the survey; no explicit write-back-trigger taxonomy (never / on-success / reflective / human-validated) is developed for the surveyed systems. [uncertain]
failure_experience_usage: Not centrally addressed. The survey covers self-correction/critique (CriticBench, Self-Correction Rate metric, SELF-RAG critique) at evaluation/mechanism level but does not develop storing/retrieving failed experiences as a memory mechanism. [uncertain]
memory_evolution_update: Not addressed as a dedicated dimension; the survey does not characterize append-only vs dedup-merge vs refine-overwrite dynamics for a growing memory store. [uncertain]
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: the survey covers learned/trainable retrievers and query rewriters and RL-trained generators (co-training, dual fine-tuning, RL frameworks), and adaptive retrieval policies (SELF-RAG). It does not frame retrieval as a formal RL policy (e.g., M-MDP soft Q-learning) -- it catalogs the shift from similarity-only to learned/adaptive retrieval.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes -- a distinctive contribution: Section 8.5 treats cross-framework/cross-agent interoperability protocols (Agent-to-Agent A2A, Agent Communication Protocol ACP, Agent Network Protocol ANP) and the 'convergence-by-layering' thesis, plus multi-agent collaboration/debate frameworks and model communication in orchestration. Shared memory across heterogeneous agents is framed as an open standardization concern.
benchmarks: RAG: Natural Questions, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, RealTimeQA, MS MARCO, BEIR, TREC-DL, OpenBookQA, PopQA, TruthfulQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, StrategyQA, SQuAD, DROP, WikiAsp, Multi-News, NarrativeQA, UniEval, Ragas, KILT. MLLM: MM-Vet, ALLaVA, SEED-Bench, ChartQA, MMC-Benchmark, DocVQA, TextVQA, MM-SafetyBench, MME, MultiBench. Orchestration: BigDataBench, AIBench Training, AISBench, WebArena, Long Range Arena, ZeroSCROLLS, AI Fairness 360. LLM Agents: RoleLLM, AgentBench, AgentBoard, AgentQuest, InfiAgent-DABench, CriticBench, ML-Bench, Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL).
benchmark_family: QA (NQ, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, SQuAD, DROP, OpenBookQA, PopQA, TruthfulQA, RealTimeQA); multi-hop (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, StrategyQA); passage retrieval (MS MARCO, BEIR, TREC-DL); RAG-pipeline (Ragas, KILT); summarization/long-form (WikiAsp, Multi-News, NarrativeQA, UniEval); multimodal (MM-Vet, SEED-Bench, ChartQA, DocVQA, TextVQA, MME, MultiBench, MM-SafetyBench); web/agent (WebArena, AgentBench, AgentBoard, AgentQuest); tool (ML-Bench, BFCL); long-context (Long Range Arena, ZeroSCROLLS); systems/orchestration (BigDataBench, AIBench, AISBench); fairness (AI Fairness 360).
baselines: N/A as a single comparison -- being a survey, it does not run head-to-head baselines. It positions itself (Table 1) against prior surveys: Lin et al. 2024, Lee et al. 2025, Bhagat et al. 2025, Li 2025, Guo et al. 2024, Yan et al. 2025, Xi et al. 2025, claiming the first full cross-axis (RAG+Agents+MLLM+Orchestration+Evaluation+Standardization) coverage.
key_metrics: Catalogs per-axis metrics: RAG -- Accuracy, F1, EM, MRR, nDCG, Precision, Recall, ROUGE, BLEU, Faithfulness, Context Precision, Context Recall. MLLM -- Accuracy, F1, EM, Perplexity, BLEU, ROUGE, custom safety metrics. Agents -- Role-Consistency Score, Self-Correction Rate, Reasoning Trace Accuracy, Generalization Score, Tool Call Accuracy, Token Efficiency. Orchestration -- Throughput, Latency Overhead, Bandwidth Utilization, Mean Task Completion Time, Avg. API Response Time, Cache Hit Rate, fairness metrics.
headline_result: As a survey there is no single empirical headline number. Headline contribution: the first unified multi-dimensional CAIS taxonomy across four axes (RAG, LLM Agents, MLLMs, Orchestration) plus evaluation and standardization (MCP/A2A/ACP/ANP), synthesizing 227 references / 220+ papers (2020-early 2026), positioned (Table 1) as the only prior work providing full cross-axis coverage.
ablations: N/A -- a survey does not run ablations. It instead provides comparative analyses: RAG retriever paradigms (sparse/dense/graph/hybrid) across latency, recall, scalability dimensions (Table 2); LLM agent reasoning-framework comparison; MLLM architecture comparison; and orchestration-framework comparison tables, which serve an analogous design-tradeoff role.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes -- the survey explicitly notes RAG evaluation targets both retrieval quality (MRR, nDCG) and generation factuality (EM, F1, ROUGE, BLEU) as separate concerns, and Ragas/KILT for end-to-end pipeline evaluation, thereby distinguishing intrinsic retrieval metrics from end-to-end task metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Beyond outcome metrics (Accuracy/EM/F1), it highlights process/intermediate metrics: Reasoning Trace Accuracy, Self-Correction Rate, Role-Consistency Score, Faithfulness/Context-Precision/Context-Recall (Ragas), and orchestration process metrics (task completion time, cache hit rate). It flags lack of unified system-level metrics as a gap.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively: RAG retriever comparison weighs retrieval latency, recall quality, and scalability (Table 2); orchestration metrics include throughput, latency overhead, API response time, cache hit rate; agent metrics include Token Efficiency; PagedAttention is cited for memory/throughput efficiency. Sustainable/efficient deployment is named as an open opportunity (Sec 10.2.6).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Not prescribed numerically; the survey notes the problem of dumping static tool schemas into the context window vs active tool discovery (Fei et al. 2025) and long-context evaluation (Long Range Arena, ZeroSCROLLS, ZeroSCROLLS), but does not specify a fixed-k or budget convention. [uncertain]
survey_scope_and_axes: Four organizing axes: (1) RAG, (2) LLM Agents, (3) Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), (4) Orchestration; plus cross-cutting Evaluation and Standardization (MCP/A2A/ACP/ANP). Formalism: CAIS = f(L, C, D). Coverage: literature search Dec 2024-May 2026 over ACM DL, arXiv, IEEE Xplore, Semantic Scholar; window 2020-early 2026; ~400 candidates screened to 220+ retained; 227 references.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A -- the survey does not construct a new benchmark; it aggregates and catalogs existing benchmarks (Table 8) and identifies the absence of unified system-level CAIS benchmarks and robust multimodal benchmarks as a key gap.
builds_on: Builds on the Berkeley AI Research (BAIR/Zaharia et al. 2024) 'Compound AI Systems' framing; foundational works it organizes include Lewis et al. 2020 (RAG), Brown et al. 2020 (GPT-3), ReAct (Yao et al. 2023), SELF-RAG (Asai et al. 2023), IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2022), ITER-RETGEN (Shao et al. 2023), REPLUG (Shi et al. 2023), Atlas (Izacard et al. 2023), and the MCP specification (Anthropic 2024).
contrasts_with: Prior surveys with narrower scope (Table 1): Lin et al. 2024 and Lee et al. 2025 (optimization-only), Bhagat et al. 2025 (info-seeking QA only), Li 2025 (agent paradigms), Guo et al. 2024 (multi-agent), Yan et al. 2025 (agent communication), Xi et al. 2025 (agent systems). It claims to be the first with full cross-axis CAIS coverage including standardization.
lineage: Surveys group. A cross-cutting CAIS taxonomy survey that links the RAG (group B), Agents/tool-use (group C), and Orchestration/multi-agent (group E) sub-topics under one f(L,C,D) framework, also covering MLLMs; positioned as an umbrella/integration survey across the retrieval-augmented LLM-agents landscape.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR framing; the survey does not discuss case adaptation/revision mechanisms)
